newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs tumble.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs tumble.

text.p: CME pork belly futures closed down the daily 3.000-cent-per-lb limit in nearby contracts and sharply lower in deferred "new crop" months as weak cash markets offset light stocks in storage.
Hog futures also tumbled sharply late on weak cash ideas and techicals before short covering pared losses, traders said.
July and August pork bellies closed limit down with July at settling at 79.175 cents per lb and August at 78.425 cents. Other months ended 1.975 to 1.725 cent lower.
Hog futures closed 1.525 cent a lb lower to 0.200 higher with August pacing the decline after falling as much as 1.800 cent before the close and settling at 80.100 cents.
Falling cash belly prices despite tight stocks weighed on on pork belly futures, traders noted.

USDA reported cash belly values slipped another $1 per cwt at noon, quoted at $85.00 for 12- to 14-lb bellies and $83.00 for 16- to 18-lb supplies. Prices will likely continue to ease as they have in the past, after hitting user resistance last week at the $90 mark, they said.
"A small amount of bellies in storage is still too much if there is no demand," one trader said.
Product availabilty is also seen increasing as shown by the last Hogs and Pigs report which indicated an expanding hog herd and slaughter rates above a year earlier into the fall.

"Everybody thinks we're just starting a big supply cycle in the hogs so no one really thinks we need a carryover (of frozen bellies) when August goes off the board," said Rich Tokheim, president of Investment Research Company.

Tokheim also cited the narrow discount of futures to cash. A discount of eight to 10 cents a lb is needed to encourage pulling of frozen product from storage and currently there is less than a four-cent discount of futures to cash, he said.
Unfilled sell orders totaled 52 in July and 80 in August.
E.D.&F. Man, Refco, Dean Witter and Iowa Grain notably sold August on the break, pit sources said.

Hog futures fell as pressure from pork bellies reinforced selling sparked by weaker cash hog indications for later this week and pushed values into sell stops. Indications were mixed for cash hogs on Tuesday but many traders expected lower cash hog prices late this week because of weakening pork prices.
Hog runs have generally been tighter than expected but demand for pork also has been running much less than anticipated for domestic use as well as for export.
Packers' margins recently sank to their lowest levels in years which may force some companies to cut kills and hope for increased hog marketings, traders said.
R.J. O'Brien, Rosenthal Collins, Cargill Investor Services and Lind-Waldock notably sold while Rand Financials was on both sides of the market late, pit sources said.
In hog options, Refco sold October 70 and 72 puts, LFG bought December 78 calls and Term Commodities bought August 77 puts early. Rosenthal bought July 83 calls late, pit sources added.
